free_tier.stated: Each year the Innovative and Novel Computational Impact on Theory and Experiment (INCITE) program awards to researchers billions of supercomputer processor hours and 100 trillion bytes of data storage space
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: No per-file ceiling is stated on the FAQ or OLCF data page; the limits are per area: 200 TB archival on Kronos and 50 TB per Orion work area.

retention.stated: OLCF does not guarantee lifetime data retention. After project end or account deactivation, data in non-purged areas is retained for 90 days, after which OLCF may delete it; Orion files not accessed for 90 days are eligible for purge.

egress.terms: Selected non-proprietary projects are not charged for access to the facilities. The pages read state no egress meter. World Archive directories are readable by any user on the OLCF system.

tooling: scp and rsync to the OLCF data transfer nodes; the 'OLCF Kronos' Globus collection; Orion Lustre work areas and the Kronos nearline archive. HPSS was decommissioned on January 31, 2025.
chaining: OLCF: a moderate project without export control restrictions gets archival space on Kronos with a default 200 TB quota shared by the project, world and user archive areas. Orion Lustre (679 PB usable) work areas have 50 TB quotas and purge files not accessed in 90 days. Whether storage is metered separately from compute is not stated on the pages read.
limits_note: Annual call from mid-April through the end of June. Awards run one to three years; multiyear awards submit annual renewal requests that undergo peer review. The facilities reserve the right to limit the amount and duration of archival storage once a project has been completed.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Tenured infrastructure; data survives, but the allocation expires and the archival quota can be clawed back after project end - treat as renewable-while-funded, not permanent.

extras.verified_at_basis: re-checked against the first-party page on 2026-11-19 (a verify run); evidence rows dated by the seed pass, which ended 2026-10-21, keep that date as an upper bound
extras.quota_verbatim: 100 trillion bytes (~100 TB) of data storage awarded across the programme each year; per-project archival quota at OLCF is 200 TB (shared across Project/World/User Archive on Kronos).
extras.limits_verbatim: Annual call only (mid-April to mid/late June), awards 1-3 years with a peer-reviewed annual renewal request. Post-project archival storage is explicitly at the facility's discretion ('The facilities reserve the right to limit the amount and duration of archival storage once a project has been completed'). Data must be research data; personal/non-work use prohibited.
extras.egress_verbatim: Globus/GridFTP and SSH transfer free to allocation holders; no egress meter. Data is not a public HTTP origin.
extras.chaining_verbatim: One allocation = one project directory on a 100+ PB Lustre (Eagle/Orion) plus up to 200 TB nearline archive. Storage is not separately metered, so a storage-heavy proposal can request a large quota against a small compute request - but the proposal must still justify compute.
extras.tooling_verbatim: SSH/scp/sftp, Globus, Lustre + HPSS/Kronos nearline mounts; no S3.
extras.agent_focus: Credit, grant and sponsorship programmes that fund storage, assessed on RENEWABILITY rather than headline size. The question is not 'how big is the credit' but 'does it come back next year, and can an unaffiliated individual outside the US/EU hold it'.

binding_note: 100 TB is awarded to projects by a review panel; there is no route from an unaffiliated individual to an allocation.
